result.topic_en: Riemann states Abel's continuity theorem for power series as a lemma and uses it to evaluate the boundary values, at q_0 = e^{xi}, of the integral of (log k − log 4√q) dq/q, distinguishing rational and irrational x/2π and odd and even denominators.
result.transcription:
Accuratiori functionum propositarum disquisitioni tanquam lemma antemittimus theorema sequens generale.
Si series $a_0+a_1+a_2+\cdots$ eo quo scripsimus ordine summata [-seriem-] {+summam+} habet convergentem functio ipsius x [?] per seriem $a_0+a_1 r+a_2 r^2\cdots$ definita convergente $r$ versus limitem 1. convergit versus valorem eundem.
Inde facile deducitur.
Si functio $f(q)$ complexae quantitatis $q$, versante modulo ipsius $q$ infra unitatem (pro modulis ipsius $q$ unitate minoribus) [-et-] exhibeatur per seriem:
$a_0+a_1 q+a_2 q^2+\cdots$
hanc seriem pro valore $q_0$ cujus modulus est unitas, si habeat summam, exprimere valorem eum, quem functio $f(q)$ assumat convergente $q$ versus $q_0$, appropinquante puncto, per quod quantitas $q$ repraesentatur in linea ad limitem spatii, in quo functio est data normali.
Quamobrem hos tantum valores functionum propositarum hic respicimus, etiamsi evolutiones 48–54 latius pateant.
Sit brevitatis gratia $(x)$ absolute minima quantitatis $x$ a numero integro distantia, aut si $x$ e numero integro et fractione $\frac12$ composita est, $=0$; porro $E(x)$ numerus integer [-absolute-] maximus non major quam $x$, obtinemus e (48), attribuendo ipsi $q$ valorem $q_0=e^{xi}$
62). $\int_0^{e^{xi}}\left(\log k-\log 4\sqrt[4]{q}\right)\frac{dq}{q} = -2\log 4\cos^2\frac{x}{2}+\frac{2}{4}\log 4\cos^2\frac{2x}{2}-\frac{2}{9}\log 4\cos^2\frac{3x}{2}+\frac{2}{16}\log 4\cos^2\frac{4x}{2}$
$-4\pi i\left(\frac{x}{2\pi}\right)+\frac{4\pi i}{4}\left(\frac{2x}{2\pi}\right)-\frac{4\pi i}{9}\left(\frac{3x}{2\pi}\right)+\frac{4\pi i}{16}\left(\frac{4x}{2\pi}\right)-\cdots$
$\left[=\sum(-1)^n\frac{\log 4\cos\frac{nx}{2}^2}{nn}-2\log 4\left(1-\frac14+\frac19-\frac1{16}\cdots\right)\quad ?\right]$
Pars imaginaria hujus seriei convergit, quicunque est valor ipsius $x$, pars realis [-f-] si $\frac{x}{2\pi}$ est numerus surdus, non convergit [quippe quum in hoc casu semper infinitas numerorum [-n-] $n$ determinari potest, per quos {+valor ipsius+} $\cos\frac{nx}{2}$ minor evadit quovis numero dato], sin minus, denotando $m,n$ numeros integros inter se primos et ponendo $\frac{x}{2\pi}=\frac{m}{n}$ ita exhiberi potest.
1° si $n$ est impar aequalis fit:
$\frac{\pi^2}{n^2}\sum_{1,n-1}^{s}(-1)^s\frac{\cos\frac{\pi s}{n}}{\sin^2\frac{\pi s}{n}}\log 4\cos\frac{sm\pi}{n}^2-\frac{\pi^2}{6n^2}\log 4$ $\qquad\left[-\frac{\pi^2}{6n^2}\log 4\right]$
[fit enim primo aequalis:
$\sum_{0,\infty}^{\kappa}\sum_{1,n-1}^{s}\frac{(-1)^{\kappa+s}}{(\kappa n+s)^2}\log 4\cos\frac{s\pi m}{n}^2+\sum_{1,\infty}^{\kappa}\sum_{0,n-1}^{s}\frac{(-1)^{\kappa-s}}{(\kappa n-s)^2}\log 4\cos\frac{s\pi m}{n}^2$
quod facile in formam supra datam redigitur, utendo formulis notis:
$\frac{1}{z^2}-\frac{1}{(\pi+z)^2}+\frac{1}{(2\pi+z)^2}-\cdots$
$-\frac{1}{(\pi-z)^2}+\frac{1}{(2\pi-z)^2}-\cdots=\frac{\cos z}{\sin^2 z}\qquad 1-\frac14+\frac19-\frac1{16}+\cdots=\frac{\pi^2}{12}$ ]
2° si $n$ est par, designando $p$ numerum imparem.
$=\frac{\pi^2}{n^2}\sum_{1,\frac n2-1}^{s}\frac{2(-1)^s\log 4\cos\frac{sm\pi}{n}^2}{\sin\frac{\pi s}{n}^2}+\frac{\pi^2}{3n^2}\log 4+\frac{2\pi^2}{n^2}(-1)^{\frac m2}\left(\log\frac{q_0-q}{q_0+q}+\log n+\frac{8}{\pi^2}\sum\frac{\log p}{p^2}\right)$
Quae formula manifesto ita est intelligenda, ut functionem propositam, subtracta functione $\frac{2\pi^2}{n^2}(-1)^{\frac m2}\log\frac{q_0-q}{q_0+q}$, si $q$ convergat versus limitem $q_0$ modo supra stabilito, convergere versus limitem finitum, ejusque valorem assignat.
[primo enim habetur, si per $f(q)$ functionem propositam denotamus.
$f(q)=2\sum_{1}^{\frac n2-1}+2\sum_{\frac n2+1}^{n-1}+2\sum_{n+1}^{\frac{3n}{2}-1}+\cdots+\log 4\frac{\pi^2}{3n^2}+\lim_{q=q_0}\frac{(-1)^{\frac m2}}{n^2}16\sum_{1,\infty}^{p}\frac{\log(1+q^{p\frac n2})}{p^2}$
Pars prior hujus expressionis fit ut supra: $\frac{\pi^2}{n^2}\sum_{1,\frac n2-1}^{s}\frac{2(-1)^s\log 4\cos\frac{sm\pi}{n}^2}{\sin\frac{\pi s}{n}^2}+\frac{\pi^2}{3n^2}\log 4$, beneficio formulae notae:
$\frac{1}{\sin^2 z}=\frac{1}{z^2}+\frac{1}{(\pi+z)^2}+\frac{1}{(\pi-z)^2}+\frac{1}{(2\pi+z)^2}+\frac{1}{(2\pi-z)^2}+\cdots$

Partial fraction expansion of cos z/sin^2 z and alternating zeta value π²/12
